title: Native open tensor presentation data and normalization predicates
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the native coefficient sheaves $B_V$, actual abelian pro-etale Weil-sheaf categories $\mathcal W_V$ and their exact open extension and module pullback functors of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], the ordinary derived categories and localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and exactly the sheaf tensor, signed direct-sum total tensor, categorical two-sided K-flatness, derived tensor and chosen K-flat tensor models of [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow Z_0$ be a $k_0$-open immersion between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. The following are data types and compatibility predicates; no existence assertion is part of this definition.

Write $E=j_!$, $R=j^*$, $D(E),D(R)$ for their exact derived functors. A native sheaf open tensor datum $s$ consists of an adjunction $E\dashv R$ whose unit and counit forget to the actual ordinary open unit and counit, invertibility of its unit, a restriction/tensor isomorphism $R(M\otimes N)\cong RM\otimes RN$ whose underlying map is the canonical balanced module comparison, and isomorphisms $EM\otimes N\cong E(M\otimes RN)$ whose inverses have adjoint transpose $(\eta_M\otimes1)$ followed by the inverse restriction comparison. It also records that both $E$ and $R$ preserve categorical two-sided K-flatness.

A native derived open tensor datum $d$ relative to $s$ consists of natural isomorphisms $\gamma:D(E)M\otimes^LN\cong D(E)(M\otimes^LD(R)N)$ and $\rho:D(R)(M\otimes^LN)\cong D(R)M\otimes^LD(R)N$. The inverse of $\gamma$ satisfies the same unit-transpose equation for the specified exact-derived adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. It includes the existence of an ordinary restriction comparison and ordinary open tensor isomorphism with this unit normalization, agreeing with $\rho,\gamma$ after forgetting Frobenius under the recorded tensor comparisons and the actual exact-functor factorization isomorphisms for $E,R$.

For abelian categories $A,B$ with chosen derived categories, an open tensor presentation $c$ records exact additive functors $E:A\to B$, $R:B\to A$, sheaf, total and derived tensor functors, K-flat predicates, preservation by $E,R$, tensor-model isomorphisms on every pair of K-flat complexes, and the total-complex summand insertion maps. It records sheaf, chain and derived open tensor comparisons and restriction/tensor comparisons. Each chain map agrees on every $(p,q)$ summand with its sheaf map; each derived map agrees on every pair of K-flat inputs with localization of its chain map under the specified models and exact-functor factors. The predicates for the unit-transpose equation, the open and restriction localization squares, the summand equations and the forgetting square are the corresponding componentwise equalities.

Define native presentation compatibility for $s,d,c$ to mean that every functor, K-flat predicate, model and insertion in $c$ equals the actual native construction, and that its sheaf and derived comparisons equal those in $s,d$. Equality of dependent presentations is heterogeneous equality. The auxiliary operations are the existing localized pullback and extension, the left-first sheaf tensor, the actual total summand insertion, the chosen K-flat tensor model, and the canonical forgetting factorization isomorphisms. For any composable $k_0$-maps $j:V\to W$, $p:W\to Y$, the auxiliary pullback compositor $D(j^*)D(p^*)\cong D((pj)^*)$ is localization of the existing balanced module compositor $b\otimes(c\otimes t)\mapsto b\,j^*(c)\otimes t$, with inverse inserting $1$. Derived comparisons have arbitrary ambient derived inputs, with no boundedness, lisse or degree-zero restriction.
